report.source_text: A pathology examination from the GEJ nodule showed squamous mucosa with mucosal ulcer and associated acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrates. Nests of atypical cohesive cells with clear cytoplasm, and mild nuclear pleomorphism were noted in submucosa. Multiple immunostains were performed to further characterize atypical cells with following staining pattern: vimentin (+), PAX-8 (+), CD10 (focally and weakly positive), and epithelial membrane antigen (EMA; focally and weakly positive) (Figs. 2, 3, 4, and 5). These cells were negative for RCC, thyroid transcription factor 1(TTF1), S100 protein, CD68, cytokeratin 5/6, pancytokeratin, p63, cytokeratin 7 and 20, p40, and pan melanoma marker. Histological features and staining patterns were consistent with atypical clear cell infiltrate involving squamous mucosa, which was consistent with metastatic RCC.

clinician.final_diagnosis: metastatic renal clear cell carcinoma involving esophageal mucosa at the gastroesophageal junction
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man presented with intermittent dysphagia to solids and substernal food sticking sensation. Physical exam was normal. EGD revealed a single 6 mm nodule at the GEJ with mild esophagitis. Biopsy of the nodule showed atypical clear cell infiltrate with immunostains supporting metastatic RCC. An expert pathology conference confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic renal clear cell carcinoma, Fuhrman grade 2, involving the esophageal mucosa with erosion. CT scan showed an unremarkable esophagus and no mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: EGD revealed a 6 mm nodule at the GEJ with Los Angeles grade A distal esophagitis.
Biopsy of the GEJ nodule showed nests of atypical clear cells with immunostain profile consistent with metastatic renal clear cell carcinoma.
Expert pathology conference confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic renal clear cell carcinoma Fuhrman grade 2 involving esophageal mucosa with erosion.
CT chest, abdomen and pelvis showed no abnormalities of the esophagus and no mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Biopsy histology and immunostains were not consistent with primary esophageal cancer or other carcinoma; CT imaging showed no mediastinal lymphadenopathy or esophageal mass beyond the GEJ nodule.

remaining_uncertainties: No documented clinical treatment approach or follow-up and outcome data are available.
